payload.body: Burrow bands of gnome scrappers scratch a living in scrub hills where thin soil defeats plows but hides warrens. They stand half a man’s height, broad-nosed and mud-caked, built low for tunnel work the empire once taxed. After the fracture left border farms unguarded, these bands traded winter labor for lifted grain and learned to fight farmers’ dogs. Ordinary folk laugh at their waddle until a whole pack boils from a ditch with picks, for numbers make them bold. They share food by strict pebble-count and exile thieves by burying them neck-deep till dawn, a justice travelers find crueler than whipping. In open battle they rush ankles with picks and hammers, brave in packs of six and cowardly alone, breaking the moment a shield-wall holds. They know every rabbit-run for miles and move camps each season, leaving swept burrows patrols find empty. Cold drives them down to storehouses, and only blocked burrows and fed dogs thin them. They roam only in small outside-society bands, with no settlement or faction implication as final content. Their pebble-count justice settles every quarrel without appeal, and exiled thieves warn others for seasons. They move their burrow camps with the seasons, leaving swept tunnels that patrols always find empty. Travellers who share bread and mind their dogs pass warren lands unmolested by night. Grey elders settle burrow quarrels by whistle-codes that carry through packed earth. Blocked burrows and fed dogs thin them faster than any spear wall. Young diggers learn pebble-count before they learn letters, counting shares in the dark. Barrow-straps creak under tool weight on every long farm lane. River-stone pouches never empty while scrub hills stand.

payload.body: Tinker gnomes push whole workshops on their backs along farm lanes, mending kettles that successor smiths charge too dear to fix. payload.body: Poacher bands live hedge-to-hedge along great farms they will never own, taking rabbits the game laws reserve for tables they never sit at. They stand half grown and move like field-mice, a craft learned from hungry childhoods after the empire’s granaries emptied. Farmers hang wire for them as for foxes, and catch them as rarely. Their short bows drop hares silently, and their snares feed whole bands through winter. When discovered they melt through streams, for water kills scent. In open fight they loose once then flee, useless against shields, frost hardens their trade and sharpens hunger. A full woodpile and a blind eye buy more peace than patrols. They roam only in small outside-society bands, with no settlement or faction implication as final content. A mended roof and a blind eye buy more peace with them than any patrol. Their caravan shares are divided by counted sticks, and every elder remembers the famine years. They prefer melting through streams to standing in line, for water kills scent and dogs. Young runners learn hedge-paths before they learn letters, moving like field-mice. Grey elders divide every caravan share by counting sticks around evening fires. Frost hardens their poaching trade and sharpens hunger through lean months. Kennel-carts roll with their bands wherever goats wander. Leaf-cloaks sewn with pockets hide snares, pipes, and supper.

payload.body: Exiles are oath-cut wanderers camped in played-out quarries, forbidden the holds they still dream of. They stand broad and low, bearded, stone-eyed, carrying the shame-tallies they never show. After the empire’s pay stopped, many sold axes to whoever fed. Villagers hire them against brutes no militia can face, they keep exile codes strictly among themselves. In battle they are solid axe-and-shield fighters who hold ground and break only when surrounded, they respect anyone who stands, work slowly buys parole-tallies. They roam only in small outside-society bands, with no settlement or faction implication as final content. They respect anyone who stands ground beside them, and slow work buys parole-tallies. Their craft is coal and bellows only, with no runic magic claimed as final. These exiles keep no holds and no clans as final content, only quarry camps and tally-sticks. Cave-ins haunt their dreams, and lantern-codes mark the bounds they guard. Young oath-cut exiles drill with hand-axes in played-out quarries each morning. Grey singers keep hammer-timing songs that synchronize whole crews without magic. Quarry dust ingrains every beard no matter how often washed. Song-tallies knotted in beards record pay-shares without writing.

In battle they roll repeatedly with gripped victims held fast, drowning even fully armored foes reliably. Their sudden death frees reaches for many years, rival elders absorb leaderless survivors quickly. These croc-folk are reasoning bands rather than animals, wholly distinct from the river crocs of the Beast roster. This one leads only a roaming band, with no wider rule or faction implication as final content. They roam only in small outside-society bands, with no settlement or faction implication as final content. Nervous fish tolls buy safe crossings through their delta channels. Open fire makes them abandon hunts and withdraw quickly. They collect boat nails from every captured vessel passing their reaches. Young floaters learn log-still ambushes before crushing jaw-sweeps. Scarred brutes erupt beside boats with sweeping tail blows. Winding reaches close under echoing roars when elders display. Barnacled armor plates elders rolling with gripped victims. Boat nails pile in collections from every captured vessel.
payload.base_appearance: Massive scarred elder carries rolling bulk and barnacled armor, jaws enormous, tail tree-thick. Breath fishy. It stands built for band warfare in open country, carrying worn working gear.
payload.portrait_brief: Head-and-shoulders interface portrait of Deathroll Elder (band-level only): slit-eyed mossy-scute armored face, steady gaze, worn headgear and band tokens, soft river delta daylight behind.

payload.body: Broad-winged stormcaller folk ride towering thunderheads high above the highest plateaus. Their crackling bands faithfully follow wandering lightning strikes each storm. They read gathering static accurately in raised feathers. Worried herders watch their circling flight for storm warnings. In battle they dive screaming through driving rain with heavy stone axes, stunning victims with crackling screeches. They cannot sustain flight in completely calm air, their lightning-split eyries smoke after every tempest. These thunderbird folk stand apart from the storm rocs of the Beast roster and from darker winged powers. Their uncanny behavior remains a flagged intuitive proposal under magic doctrine, never cast as final magic. They roam only in small outside-society bands, with no settlement or faction implication as final content. Their storm-screech is flagged as an intuitive behavior-magic proposal, never cast as final magic. They cannot sustain flight in completely calm air. Their lightning-split eyries smoke after every passing tempest. Scarred callers read gathering static accurately in raised feathers. Storm-glass charms crackle on every veteran of the colonies. Young riders learn thunderhead riding before stone axes. Storm-drums boom rolling signals across crowded storm colonies. Lightning-charms blacken on weary elders after violent gales.
